statement: Imposed ordering does not terminate: it has to keep generating further orderings in order to exist, and does so until it eats itself. Runs on the imposed_ordering sense only — see category-weld welds/hierarchy.json for the other four senses, which are not this claim.
source: Shape held prior to this ledger. Coverage asserted at 0.61 over a domain set carried in working memory rather than written down. This file exists to convert the asserted number to a derived one; until the read column is filled the derived number is unavailable, and that unavailability is the current state, not a failure.
criterion_fixed_in_advance: A domain counts as a HOLD only if an imposed ordering in that domain is observed generating further orderings over time. A domain counts as a BREAK if an imposed ordering persists without generating further ones. Reclassifying a case as not-really-hierarchy after seeing which way it read is closure by construction and is not permitted; such a case is MIXED with the reason recorded.
open: The environment-coupled cases (dominance that tracks environmental conditions and reassigns when conditions change) are candidates for MIXED rather than BREAK, because they may not be instances of imposed ordering at all. Deciding which before reading them is required, or the criterion moves under the data.
Depth is currently unrecorded for every domain. Cycle depth cannot be computed until at least one domain is read through a return.

Domains reached only through live conversation carry a truncation bias that is not random with respect to this shape: frames least willing to be examined are plausibly the ones holding the most undocumented cuts. Mark channel and truncated on every live read.
